newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dow jitters to cap S.African share gains next week.
newsitem.headline: Dow jitters to cap S.African share gains next week.

text.p: Continued strength in industrial and financial sectors is expected to boost South African shares next week, but any confident strides up are seen capped by edginess about continued volatility on Wall Street.
Dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday stock moves will also be inhibited by the three-day holiday-shortened week.

"The biggest factor is uncertainty... what is very clear is the volatility on the Dow which would indicate that there is an enormous amount of uneasiness here," said Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager at Infinity Asset Management.
The Dow Jones industrial index this week recorded its second biggest daily point gain, soaring 173 points on Tuesday.
The closely watched index, after losing almost 700 points in a month-long decline since closing at a record high of 7,085.16 on March 11, has now recouped more than 400 points.

"But at the end of the day, the underpin to the South African market is more positive than the offshore markets... our trend is still upward particularly in the financials and industrials," Graham-Parker added.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's financial 100 index this week rose to record highs buoyed by positive sentiment and good earnings prospects, although analysts said the sector was nearing its peak. Other propelling factors include an over-correction last year and a number of mergers in the sector. Dealers said robust results from industrial companies, a raft of which are expected next month, and bullishness on the futures market were also positives for shares.

"I expect once we get over this silly holiday season it will go firmer...the futures traders are definitely bullish and the spot will follow," said Greg Amoils, a director of portfolio management at Irish & Menell Rosenberg.
Financial markets are closed on Monday and Thursday next week for Freedom Day and Workers Day respectively.

However, topping up concerns about the Dow Jones, would be fresh worries about a delay in cutting local interest rates -- or even a possible rate hike this year -- following comments from Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals on Friday.
Stals said that a more restrictive monetary policy might be needed to curb recent higher credit demand and money supply trends. The comments pushed yields on the bond market higher.
March money supply and credit figures are due out at 1500 GMT and will be eyed closely, traders said.

Gold shares were seen eyeing the bullion price for direction next week, with little further downside expected on poor first quarter results which have been released since last week. "The market has probably, from as early as February this year, been discounting these (quarterly) numbers," Graham-Parker said.

Market watchers said the recent increase in the number of asset swap deals, a mechanism enabling institutions in South Africa -- limited by foreign exchange controls -- to invest abroad, would continue next week and beyond.
The March budget also increased the amount of funds institutions can invest overseas.

Company results to be watched by the market in the week ahead include year earnings from Power Technologies Ltd and half year results from Afrox Ltd. On the economics side, April gold and foreign exchange reserves are due out and seen rising towards the 14 billion rand mark.
